newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade, dealers said on Thursday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. November consumer price index (CPI), weekly jobless claims and November retails sales data.
The consumer price index for November is forecast to be unchanged from October's increase of 0.3 percent.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended December 7 is expected to be around 341,000 against 336,000 reported in the previous week.
Retail sales for November is expected to rise about 0.3 percent from 0.2 percent in October.

"The market was quietly steady in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the (U.S. November) CPI, weekly jobless claims and (U.S. November) retail sales figures," a local dealer said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday, weekend and week-fixed were unchanged from Wednesday's common 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, six-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and nine-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Twelve-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent.
